absent: Full type definitions of eventpoll, epitem, ep_pqueue, ep_ctl_ctx, epoll_key and epoll_event beyond observed fields.
Implementations of hook detachment, scan start and completion, safe wakeup, reference acquisition, upwards depth handling and wakeup presence tests.
Numeric values of maximum nesting depth, maximum user watches and private, exclusive and wakeup related event bits beyond observed use.
Busy poll and NAPI identifier handling and interrupt resume behaviour.
Breakpoint ioctl behaviour and compatibility pointer ioctl handling.
Power stay awake and relax accounting details.
Check list construction and lifetime for reverse validation.
Allocator, wait queue, RCU, mutex, spinlock and warning internals owned by other dossiers.

findings.text: A file closure helper detaches every remaining interest that watches the closing file, taking the owning context guard for each item in turn and dropping a context reference after each detachment until the watcher set is empty.

Poll context files dispatch through a common operations table covering release cleanup, readiness polling, parameter ioctls, nonseekable positioning and compatibility ioctl handling, with a diagnostic listing operation available when process filesystem support is present.

Polling a poll context joins its poll wait queue and then scans promoted interests under guard, reporting input availability when any scanned member currently satisfies its stored mask and otherwise discarding false promotions while relaxing power accounting.

Per interest readiness sampling pins the target, uses the stored mask as the poll key, delegates to ordinary file polling or recursively to nested context polling, masks the result by the stored interest, and treats a vanished target as not ready.
Parameter ioctls on poll contexts first validate that the file is a poll context and then forward two breakpoint parameter commands to a dedicated handler, rejecting every other command as invalid.
Releasing a poll context file wakes poll waiters, detaches all hooks and all interests under guard, and then drops the creation reference, freeing the context when the last reference goes away.
A context whose reference count reaches zero is expected to hold no interests; teardown asserts this emptiness and warns when the expectation is violated.
Detachment outside closure requires successfully pinning the watched file; pin failure means closure owns the item so the caller returns early without touching tree or file linkage.
Removing the final watcher of a file publishes a null watcher head so later closure can take a fast path, and for ordinary files reclaims the head container when it is unchained.

Per user watch accounting is checked against a configured maximum before allocation, incremented on success and decremented on teardown or allocation failure, with distinct failures for quota exhaustion and memory exhaustion.
New links are rejected when reverse traversal exceeds a maximum depth or when per level back path counts exceed configured limits, while top level paths are exempt from counting.
Diagnostic iteration walks interests in key order under guard, emitting one line per interest, and stops early once the output channel reports overflow, defined as filled capacity.
Poll table setup records the supplied queue callback and by default enables the full event set.
Interest lookup searches the cached tree by comparing target keys, descending left or right until an equal key is found or the search reaches an empty child.

Poll hook attachment selects exclusive versus shared waiting according to the exclusive interest flag and signals hook allocation failure through a cleared queue context that callers convert into rollback.
Tree insertion orders interests by target key and maintains cached leftmost information so ordered iteration starts at the smallest key.
File attachment reuses the existing watcher head when present, otherwise lazily allocates and publishes one head exactly once under guard, then links the new watcher for read side traversal.

A per context mutex serialises tree membership, file linkage changes, scan batches, diagnostic walks and drain loops, with nested contexts acquired in a defined order and several helpers requiring the guard on entry.

A per file spin guard protects watcher head publication and membership, while an interrupt safe per context spin guard protects ready linkage, overflow chaining and wakeup decisions, with file and context guards acquired in separate short critical sections.

Read copy update protects watcher linkage during reverse validation and protects wakeup pointer publication, with deferred reclaim after unlink and an explicit grace wait before unregistering destroyed wakeup sources.

Interest modification updates the stored mask and data before sampling readiness and issues a full ordering barrier in between, pairing with callback locking and sleeper checks so neither fresh nor past readiness is missed.

Observed context state includes a reference count, cached tree root, mutex, interrupt safe spin guard with sequence counter, two wait queues for event and poll waiters, a ready list, an overflow marker, an owner identity, a wakeup source and a reverse reference head.

Observed interest state includes an owning context pointer, a target descriptor key, an event mask with user data, a tree node, a ready link, a file linkage node, a poll hook list, a wakeup pointer shared with deferred reclaim storage, and overflow chaining.

Context lifetime starts with a single creation reference, gains one reference per successful registration, loses one per detachment and per release cleanup, and frees resources through deferred reclaim once the final put observes zero.

Interest lifecycle proceeds from quota checked allocation to file attachment and tree insertion, then optional wakeup registration and hook attachment with immediate promotion when already ready, followed by later modification or callback promotion and finally hook detachment with deferred reclaim.

Readiness handling promotes an interest to the ready list when idle, chains it to an overflow set when a scan is in flight for later requeue, and suppresses promotion when the interest retains only private bits after one shot disabling.

Closure teardown first wakes poll waiters when present, then under guard detaches every poll hook and then every interest with scheduling pauses during long walks, before releasing the creation reference.
Detachment racing with file closure is resolved by pinning: only the side that obtains a pin proceeds with unlink, so closure cannot miss an item and detachment cannot free an item owned by closure.

Target teardown during callback unlinks the wait entry with an operation tolerant of a second deletion and publishes a null hook head with release ordering, allowing concurrent hook removal that already observed a non null head to serialise safely.
Reverse validation tolerates concurrent deletion because deletions only remove links and therefore cannot inflate back path counts, keeping validation conservative without blocking deleters.

Insertion performs nesting validation after linkage and removes the new interest when validation fails; hook allocation failure and wakeup registration failure follow the same rollback with quota and reference cleanup.
Wakeup source destruction nulls the pointer first, waits for read side power accounting to finish, and only then unregisters, preventing use after free from in flight callbacks.
Allowed back path counts by nesting level are five ordered values: one thousand then five hundred then one hundred then fifty then ten.

Poll context readiness is reported with the input bit together with the normal read bit; quota exhaustion reports no space, hook and context allocation failures report no memory, and invalid nesting or invalid ioctl commands report invalid argument.
Diagnostic lines for each interest report target descriptor number, interest mask, user data, file position, inode number and device identifier.
